# Professional Document Designer

Apply professional formatting standards appropriate to the document type. Identify the document type first, then follow the corresponding reference guide.

## Document Type Detection

| What they ask for | Type | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Google Doc, report, brief, proposal, one-pager | Long-form doc | `references/google-docs.md` |
| Slides, deck, presentation, PowerPoint, ChatGPT image prompt for slides | Slides | `references/slides.md` |
| Email, outreach, follow-up, cold email, LinkedIn message | Email/messaging | `references/email.md` |
| One-pager, leave-behind, sell sheet, datasheet | Sales collateral | `references/one-pager.md` |
| Executive summary, board update, forecast brief | Executive doc | `references/google-docs.md` + executive section |

## Core Principles (all document types)

1. **Hierarchy first.** Every document has one primary message. Everything else supports it. If the reader can't identify the main point in 5 seconds, restructure.
2. **Whitespace is design.** Dense text signals poor design. Use headers, spacing, and short paragraphs. Never fill space for the sake of it.
3. **Scannable before readable.** Structure for the reader who skims first. Headers, bullets, bold callouts, and tables should tell the full story before anyone reads a paragraph.
4. **Match formality to audience.** Board deck ≠ internal Slack message. Prospect proposal ≠ internal report. Ask: who reads this and what do they already know?
5. **Consistency over creativity.** Use one font size for each heading level. One bullet style per list. One table format per doc. Consistency signals professionalism.
6. **Length matches purpose.** One-pagers stay one page. Executive summaries stay under one page. Reports have sections. Never pad to fill space; never truncate to seem brief.

## When Brand Guidelines Are Available

If a brand skill is loaded or brand guidelines are provided, apply brand colors, fonts, and logo placement on top of the structural formatting from the type-specific reference. Brand applies to aesthetics; structure applies regardless.

## Reference Files

- `references/google-docs.md` — Long-form docs, reports, briefs, proposals
- `references/slides.md` — Slide decks, presentation structure, image prompts
- `references/email.md` — Email, outreach, LinkedIn, follow-ups
- `references/one-pager.md` — Sales one-pagers, leave-behinds, sell sheets
